items.line: gabe des Talmuds, die צפורת כרמים als eine Heuschreckenart aus
items.note: The Talmudic term for this locust is the 'vineyard bird' (Chullin 65a). Both the defective spelling צפורת and the plene ציפורת are attested. The 19th-century scholarly convention favours the defective form, but this is a guess between two valid spellings.

items.line: Schluß. צפורת כרמים scheint uns die Heuschreckenart Gryl-
items.note: The Mishnah (Shabbat 90b) spells the term defectively, צפורת כרמים, and a 19th-century author likely followed that. The plene ציפורת is also a valid spelling, so this is not certain.

items.note: This is likely a foreign (Arabic or Romance) gloss quoted from Aruch, which I cannot verify. Either spelling is plausible; I lean towards the simpler spelling פליה without the doubled yod.

items.line: chen. — Sie mag wegen ihres schnellen Auffliegens צפורת „Vogel“
items.note: The next line prints צפורת כרמים in defective spelling, so the same form is likely here. Both spellings are valid for 'Vogel', so this is not certain.

items.note: The phrase means 'a woman ... anoints herself with it and is healed', which requires the verb מתרפא (hitpael of רפא, 'is healed'). The other reading, מחרפא, is not a word; it is a ח/ת confusion.

items.line: Von einem im Mittelalter verfaßten Gedichte (des שלמה דפיירה), wel-
items.note: The poet is Solomon de Piera, a medieval Spanish Hebrew poet, whose name is written שלמה דפיירה with ד for 'de'. רפיירה is a ד/ר misreading.

items.line: כרגע נקבצו מקרים ובאו בדי ארבה וצפורת כרמים
items.note: The line quotes Judges 6:5, 'ובאו כדי ארבה לרב' ('they came like locusts in multitude'), so the printed word is כדי; בדי would not fit this sense.

items.note: The paragraph is about the biblical locust name סלעם (Lev. 11:22), which Onkelos renders as רשונא. The reading כלעם is an OCR confusion of ס with כ and is not the word in question.

items.note: The Gemara in Nidda 25a reads 'תחלת ברייתו' ('the beginning of its formation'), and Tosafot's heading takes that word, matching 'am Anfang seiner Entstehung'. חתלת is not a fitting word here.

items.note: Chulin 62b names the birds after Shavur (Shapur), spelled שבור. Reading B is a garbled multi-word span with errors, including שכור for שבור.

items.line: tung steht der Name שפן (§. 152) nicht entgegen, da es durchaus unwahr-
items.note: The passage concerns the Hebrew animal name שפן (shafan, hyrax/coney), which was popularly linked to the name of Spain. שפנן is not an attested form.

items.note: Lev. 11:22 spells it defectively, חרגל, which fits the biblical citation. However, the plene rabbinic spelling חרגול is also plausible here.

items.note: The Chulin 65a list of local names for the locust includes רשון, which matches the German context here. רשין is not attested as a name for it.

items.note: The standard text of Chulin 65 reads ערצוביא for this חרגול‑type locust. A defective spelling ערצביא is also plausible, so this is not certain.

items.note: Chulin 65b lists כרספת (karsefet) with the chargol, and the comparison to Greek Chrysophaes requires a פ (ph). כרסכת is not an attested word.

items.note: In Chullin 65a the חגב is glossed as גדיאן, and Jastrow lists gadyan as a locust species; the Aruch spelling is גדיין. The ר in reading A is a ד/ר OCR confusion.

items.line: רזבנית (Chulin 65, a), sie ist demnach zu essen gestattet; über die Kör-
items.note: רזבנית is the locust species listed in Chulin 65a (Jastrow s.v.). The next line of the passage also prints רזבנית, while רובניה is not a known word.

items.line: perbildung der חגב, in welcher die רזבנית ihr gleich sein muß, s. §. 377.
items.note: Chulin 65a lists רזבנית as a locust species, and the earlier line of the passage also reads רזבנית. רובניה is not attested and is an ז→ו / ת→ה misread.

items.line: 65, b); im Talm. jerus. Sabbat 3, b heißt unsere Heuschrecke חלזון.
items.note: חלזון is the standard rabbinic spelling. The plene form חלוזון could occur in a Yerushalmi citation, so this is a guess.

items.line: Gattung der חגב“ (§. 384). Es heißt dort: Die איילא קמצא ist
items.note: Lewysohn derives the name from איל, so the plain spelling אילא fits the Aramaic phrase cited from Avodah Zarah 37a. The plene spelling איילא is also possible, so this is not certain.

items.note: The Talmudic locust name is usually spelled אילא קמצא (Chullin 65a), and Buxtorf's entry falls under the defective spelling איל. 'Hirsch' (stag) is spelled either איל or אייל, so both readings are possible.

items.line: 62, b), חילפי übersetzt Raschi auch hier durch אורטאוש, Ortie, und
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for nettle ('orties') is more plausibly spelled אורטאיש, with yod giving the -i-/-ie- vowel; אורטאוש fits the French less well. This is a guess, not checked against the printed text.

items.line: aram. Wort scheint aus בא und כרז zusammengesetzt zu sein und heißt:
items.note: His gloss „Der Rufer kömmt“ points to the Aramaic root כרז ('to proclaim', as in כרוזא, herald); כרו is not a word meaning 'Rufer'. However, כרו is the literal letter segment of כרובא before בא, so B remains possible.

items.line: ist. — Für כרובא haben manche Ausgaben jener Paraphrase כרובא,
items.note: The variant reading is glossed as 'Wickelraupe' from כרוך ('to wrap'), so it should be כרוכא. But the line holds two near-identical words, and the first may properly be כרובא, so which word is marked is uncertain.

items.line: כירבי für כרבי, was „Schutthaufen“ heißen soll, und כרוי sollen Am-
items.note: The passage contrasts Aruch's reading with קרבי/כרבי, so the variant should be a close spelling of the same word. כירבי fits that pattern, while כירי ('stoves') would be a different word with no link to 'Schutthaufen'. This is inferred from the context, not checked against the Aruch itself.

items.line: Wort von הסל „abfressen“ ab**). — Die Stabheuschrecke (Bacillus)
items.note: חסיל derives from the root חסל, "to devour" (Deut 28:38 יחסלנו). הסל is not a word and is an ח/ה OCR confusion.

items.line: (kurzer Weg, compendiaria), so entspricht auch מוף, Memphis; חוף, τύμπα-
items.note: תוף (drum) corresponds to Greek τύμπανον, the example of a lost μ. חוף means 'shore', which does not fit the comparison.

items.line: ν in ם eingeschoben, z. B. קומקמא (Kessel, cucuma, κουκκούμιον), פרמביא
items.note: The line says a mem is inserted, as in קומקמא, פרמביא and סימפין. Cited in isolation the letter would normally be printed as medial מ, but final ם is also possible, so this is a guess.

items.line: (Halster, φορβεία), סימפין, Rohr, σίφων).
items.note: Rabbinic סימפון (tube, pipe; cf. סימפונות, the bronchial tubes) renders σίφων, with an inserted mem. סימפין is not an attested form; the OCR likely confused ו with י.

items.line: Heuschrecke וחל, welche auch אסקרין heißt; sie wird ohne Springfüße
items.note: The locust in Chullin 65a is זחל (zachal), and Lewysohn glosses it as "kriechen" (to creep), which is the Hebrew root זחל. The reading וחל is not this word.

items.line: und ist nur die Uebersetzung von וחל „kriechen“; wir haben demnach
items.note: The gloss „kriechen“ (to crawl) points to זחל, the usual Hebrew verb for crawling, so B's first word fits and A's וחל looks like a ז/ו misread. Neither reading matches the printed line exactly: A adds מין גוזי and B adds נין, so this is not certain.

items.line: (Schachrit des 7. Pessachtages s. v. חסדי ד' אוכיר) das Wort durch: „Erd-
items.note: The phrase is Isa. 63:7, חסדי ה' אזכיר ("I will recall the kindnesses of the LORD"), which opens a piyyut. ד' is the standard abbreviation for the divine name, so reading B's ר is a ד/ר misread and A carries that ד correctly. But B's אזכיר is the real word, while A's אוכיר is a ז/ו error and not a word.

items.line: zu Nidda 63, a s. v. חנא). Für die Krankheit in Folge des Skor-
items.note: Tosafot catchwords (s.v.) often begin with תנא, which introduces a baraita. חנא is only a personal name and is not a plausible catchword here, so ח for ת looks like an OCR confusion.

items.line: kanntlich vor dem After des Skorpions. Vergl. וביב נושכת בצירעה (Raschi zu
items.note: Reading A, וביב נושכת בצירעה, is a coherent phrase ("stings like a hornet", Rashi on Chulin 58b). Reading B misreads ו as כ and ו/ת as ח, and wrongly pulls in ליעקציה, which belongs to the next citation.

items.line: Schlange an: דמחייא והורה דמחייא, daß er den Stich mehrmals wiederholt.
items.note: The Yerushalmi passage says the scorpion strikes, then 'returns' (חוזרת) and strikes again, which matches 'wiederholt'. והורה ('and taught/instructed') makes no sense in this context.

items.line: עקרב שבחדייב (Sabbat 121, b). Aruch liest הדייב, welche Lese-
items.note: Shabbat 121b has עקרב שבחדייב (Adiabene), so ב (not כ) is correct. Aruch's variant is הדייב (Hadyab) with ד; B's הרייב with ר is not a known reading.

items.line: בוכיא (Succa 52, a), Raschi erklärt: Es ist die עכביש oder אורניא,
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for 'araignée' is usually spelled with a yod for the 'ai' sound, which favours אוריניא. But the two readings differ only by one yod, and OCR can easily drop or add one, so this is a guess.

items.line: 36, col. 1036) hat daher auch die Leseart קופרים (Igel, §. 134) für
items.note: The gloss 'Igel' (hedgehog) matches biblical קפוד and rabbinic קופד/קיפוד, whose plural is קופדים. קופרים is a ד/ר misreading and is not the hedgehog word.

items.line: קופין, Affen. Es könnte aber die Leseart קופין beibehalten bleiben,
items.note: The same line repeats the word as קופין ('die Leseart קופין beibehalten'). The Talmud passage on raising animals to clear mice (Bava Kamma 80a) also spells 'apes' plene as קופין, so B looks like a dropped ו.

items.line: befestigt (Uxin 3, 10). Wenn man die Honigtafeln (חליות דבש) aus
items.note: Mishnah Uktzin 3:11 has חלות דבש, 'honeycombs', which matches 'Honigtafeln'. חליות means vertebrae and is the wrong word here.

items.line: קירותא (Κηρὸς) erklärt (Sabbat 20, b), und קירה (Cera, Jebamoth
items.note: Lewysohn glosses the Talmudic wax word (Shabbat 20b) with Greek κηρός. The single-vav form קירותא is the more usual Aramaic spelling, but a double-vav plene spelling cannot be ruled out from memory.

items.line: גוין steht gewöhnlich neben צירעין (Hornissen), wird aber von
items.note: Reading A (גוין) appears throughout the passage, and as a plural in -ין it fits the pairing with צירעין. The Talmudic word in Shabbat 106b is usually spelled גזין, so neither reading matches exactly; A is the closer and more consistent form, but this is uncertain.

items.line: Raschi als Heuschreckenart erklärt. Sabbat 106, b sagt derselbe: גוין
items.note: Every other occurrence in the passage reads גוין, the plural form used for this insect (cf. Talmudic גזין, wasps). גוזי lacks the final nun, so it looks like a misread.

items.line: er: גוין und צירעין sind Arten von ארבה; schon die Variation über
items.note: Reading A (גוין) matches the spelling used in every other line of the passage. The Talmudic term is properly גזין (Shabbat 106b), so the print may differ slightly. Reading B (גוזי) lacks the plural ending -ין and fits neither form.

items.line: גוין, die bald zu חגב (§. 384), bald zu ארבה (§. 373) gezählt wer-
items.note: The passage consistently prints גוין (the insect named beside צירעין in Berachoth/Bechoroth, cf. Talmudic גזין). גוזי breaks the plural ‑ין form used in every other line, so it is an OCR error.

items.line: schreckenart zu erklären, berechtigt zur Annahme, daß auch גוין zu dem
items.note: Every other occurrence in the passage reads גוין, paired with צירעין (the Talmudic 'honey of gazin and tziraʿin'). The plural ending ־ין fits this pairing; גוזי lacks it and is not the form used here.

items.line: heißt aber nur דבש הצירעים, und der der Wespen nur דבש הגוין; es
items.note: In the Talmudic list (Shabbat 106b, Bechorot 7b) the wasp word is gazin/guzin, spelled גזין or גוזין. Reading B's גוזין is an attested variant; reading A's גוין is not a word, though both readings may garble an original גזין.

items.line: ערעיתא (Sabbat 80, b). — Für den Frauennamen דבורה setzt der
items.note: ערעיתא fits the Aramaic feminine ending -ita, like זיבוריתא in the same line, as a term for hornet/wasp at Sabbat 80b. This is from memory and the ו/י confusion is common, so it is uncertain.

items.line: Festsetzung eines Testamentes Zeit erübrigen will, sehr scharfen (אינגרא,
items.note: OCR is more likely to drop a letter than add one, and the form with nun resembles a word-form I seem to recall from the Avodah Zarah 12b passage, but I could not verify this. Reading B, without the nun, is closer to the French 'aigre' he compares, so both remain possible.

items.line: — In unserer Talmudstelle stehen צירעה שבנינוה und זבוב שבארץ
items.note: The phrase is זבוב שבארץ מצרים, "the fly that is in the land of Egypt". It parallels צירעה שבנינוה just before it, which uses the same ש + ב construction. שכארץ ("that is like the land") makes no sense here.

items.line: חפושית entspricht dem arab. خُنْفَسآء*).
items.note: The printed forms are חפושית and the Aramaic חיפושתא (beetle, cf. A. Zara 28b). Reading B's חפושיח and חיפושחא are not words; they come from the common OCR confusion of ת with ח.

items.line: גמלניתא (transponirt aus μέγαλον; sieh ausführlich §. 355) erklärt
items.note: The word on the marked line is גמלניתא, spelled with ת as elsewhere in the passage, so A is right there; B's גמלניחא is not a word. However, Rashi's 'groß' is גסה, which supports B's second word, so neither reading is fully right.

items.line: Das arab. ن geht in den aram. Wörtern verloren, so ist קפור (§. 134)
items.note: Arabic qunfudh (hedgehog) corresponds to קפוד, and khinzir (pig) corresponds to חזיר. קפור and חויר are OCR confusions of ד/ר and ז/ו.

items.line: In unserer Stelle heißt das Fett חרבא (s. §. 92); allein eigentliches
items.note: Aramaic תרבא means 'fat, suet' (Hebrew חלב), which matches 'das Fett'; חרבא means 'sword' or 'ruin' and does not fit.

items.line: Rappoport in der dem ער גל vorangehenden Abhandlung, S. 43) behauptet, daß
items.note: This refers to the book גל עד (Gal-Ed), the Prague gravestone inscriptions, which opens with Rapoport's essay. The title is Genesis 31:47; ער גל is not a title.

items.line: Species im Talmud gemeint sei. Sie heißen allgemein חולעת (Mid-
items.note: The printed text is probably תולעת דרני: תולעת is 'worm' (Middoth 2,5) and דרני is the woodworm word cited for Sabbat 102b. Each reading has one error. A has the common ח/ת look-alike slip but keeps the correct דרני. B drops a letter from דרני to give רני, which is not the word cited. So A is closer, but neither matches exactly.

items.line: er: יחוש שבכלים. — Das erste Wort bezeichnet auch sonst kleine
items.note: The Talmudic phrase is 'gnats in the kelisin' (יבחושין שבכליסין), a legume. This matches Rashi's gloss מין קטנית and Mussaphia's derivation from Greek ὦχρος. Reading A, שבכלים ('in vessels'), looks like ס misread as final ם. The exact printed ending is uncertain, so this is not confident.

items.line: durch: מין קטנית צידראש „eine Art Erbsen, Ciceres.“ Dieses Wort
items.note: The Talmud (Hullin 67) has יבחושין שבכליסין, so כליסין in B fits, and אכלסין fits Greek ὦχρος. But A's קטנית is the usual Rashi spelling, so the readings are mixed.

items.line: Schirim fol. 1, col. 3) das Sprüchwort: מה ילדת חיפושיתה קרוצי בישי
items.note: The plural קרוצי calls for the plural adjective בישי ('worse than it'), which fits the Aramaic proverb as cited. The singular ביש is less fitting here, but I am not certain of the exact printed form.

items.line: חיפושיתה übersetzt Matnat Kehuna fälschlich durch Skorpion (שקרפיון),
items.note: Matnat Kehuna typically gives vernacular glosses in Hebrew letters, and שקרפיון renders German 'Skorpion'. עקרפין is not a known word and looks like an OCR blend with עקרב.

items.line: son identificirt דירה mit סלמנטין, jedoch unrichtig; s. §. 422. — Ueber
items.note: This is a guess: I cannot verify Simson's exact spelling. סלמנטין looks like the more common rabbinic form, perhaps linked to the salamander name. סלמונטין, with plene vav, is plausible too.

items.line: חולעת שבעיקרי גפנים „Wurm am Stamme des Weinstocks;“ es ist
items.note: תולעת means 'worm' (Chullin 67b: תולעת שבעיקרי גפנים), matching Lewysohn's gloss „Wurm“; חולעת is not a word, just a ח/ת OCR confusion.

items.line: Oelbeerbaumes als verbotenes Insect betrachtet wird, er heißt: חולעת
items.note: The Hebrew word for 'worm' is תולעת (tola'at), as in Chullin 67b's תולעת שבזיתים. The reading חולעת is not a word; it comes from confusing ח with ת.

items.line: שבעיקרי זחים „Wurm am Stamme der Oelbäume.“ — Auch dieses
items.note: Neither reading is clean. 'שבעיקרי' ("in the roots of") is the expected form, while 'שלעיקרי' looks like a misread. A's 'זחים' reads like a ח/ת confusion for 'זתים' (olives), which is the more typical OCR slip. The spelling איילא vs אילא is uncertain, so this is a guess.

items.line: חולעת שבחמרים — erst später in sie gerathen sein (Chulin 58, b),
items.note: The phrase means 'worm in dates', i.e. תולעת שבתמרים (tola'at, worm; tamar, date). Reading A's חולעת and שבחמרים come from the common ח/ת confusion and give no meaningful word here.

items.line: denden Würmer: וזין שבערשים, was Raschi durch כוצנש, Cossons,
items.note: Chullin 67b has זיזין שבעדשים, and B correctly reads שבעדשים (A has ר for ד). B's זיז also fits Landau's 'Bewegung' etymology (cf. זיז שדי). However, neither reading gets the first word (זיזין) right, and A's כוצנש matches 'Cossons' better than B's כוצוש.

items.line: sagt Raschi: Es sind dies die כוצנס, Cossons, welche in Bohnen
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss here is 'cosson' (weevil), which Hebrew script renders as כוצנ"ש / כוצנס; the passage itself gives 'Cossons'. Reading B, כוזעי, does not transcribe that word.

items.line: ein Wurm (חולעתא) fiel, welchen jenes Thier sogleich fing und ver-
items.note: Reading A's ובזבזין matches Lewysohn's own comment on the word זבזין, while B's וכבוזין and ובהגנין do not. However, the Talmudic word for worm is תולעתא, which favours B's first word, so neither reading is fully right.

items.line: ובזבזין ובהגזין ובשקצים וברמשים; das Wort זבזין wird wohl aus זבזבין cor-
items.note: The sentence reads: "das Wort זבזין wird wohl aus זבזבין corrumpirt sein" (the word zbzyn is probably a corruption of zbzbyn). Reading A gives exactly these two words, the attested form and its proposed emendation. Reading B (זבוזין וכוביז) is garbled and is not meaningful Hebrew or Aramaic.

items.line: הה דרימוני (Sabbat 90, b) identisch, welches Insect zu verschlingen
items.note: Reading A has the correct spelling for 'of pomegranates' (as in the pomegranate worm of Shabbat 90b); B's רימיני looks like a ו/י confusion. The second word in both readings is unclear, so this is not certain.

items.line: natürliche Fäulniß übergegangene Saat der Ausdruck החליע gebraucht
items.note: Kilayim 2:3 has 'עד שתתליע' (let the sown seed rot or become wormy), from the root תלע, hiphil התליע, which fits 'natural decay'. החליע is not a word with this meaning.

items.line: זבוב (Nidda 25, a), דורבא (Berachoth 44, a), pl. דידבי (Nidda
items.note: The Aramaic word for fly is דידבא, with the plural דידבי (Nidda 17a). The form דידבתא cited right after it in the passage supports the reading דידבי; דירבי is a ד/ר misreading.

items.line: Fliegen durch Affen s. §. 401. — Ueber זבזין, s. S. 311, Anmerkung.
items.note: A cross-reference to a note on another page suggests a distinct, unusual lemma. זבזין fits that better than the construct plural זבובי, which is odd standing alone. I could not confirm the word against a source.

items.line: יבחושין, Raschi erklärt: כמין יתושים דקין הנמצאות במרתפות של יין „eine

items.note: The Talmudic phrase (Beitzah 32b, Pesachim 113b) is "those whose lives are not lives", built on חייהן "their lives". חיין is a rarer, shortened variant that remains possible.
